title: Governments Invest $71.8B in Space Defense as Militarization of Space Accelerates
html:
Paris, France | November 2026 — Novaspace’s Space Defense & Security, 2nd Edition finds that governments invested approximately $71.8 billion in space defense and security activities globally in 2025, reflecting the growing importance of space as a military domain and a critical component of modern multi-domain operations.

Despite 49 countries having invested at least $10 million in space defense and security capabilities, global spending remains highly concentrated. The United States, China, Russia, Japan, and France accounted for approximately 90% of space defense and security expenditure in 2025, highlighting both the strategic importance and increasing competitiveness of the sector.

As geopolitical competition intensifies, governments are accelerating investments in capabilities that support sensing, communications, navigation, intelligence, decision-making, and military operations across land, air, sea, cyber, and space domains.

“Governments no longer view space solely as supporting operations on Earth. Space itself is becoming operationally contested,” notes Rachel Hughes, Novaspace Senior Consultant. “From Secure SatCom and Space Domain Awareness to Counterspace and Missile Defense, investments increasingly reflect the reality that future military advantage will depend on freedom of action in space.”

Of the $71.8B invested globally in 2025, approximately $33.6B was contracted to industry. Secure SatCom, Counterspace, and Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance represented the largest areas of government procurement, reflecting demand for resilient communications and intelligence-driven military operations.

The shift toward hybrid sovereign-commercial architectures continues as governments combine national and commercial capabilities to enhance resilience, accelerate deployment, and strengthen flexibility. Strategic advantage increasingly depends on securing reliable access to capabilities, rather than ownership alone.

“The most successful defense organizations will be those that can combine commercial innovation with sovereign capabilities to deliver space-enabled military advantage at speed,” adds Hughes.

About the Report
Space Defense & Security, 2nd Edition delivers a comprehensive assessment of government expenditures, industry revenues, policy developments, and capability trends across the global space defense ecosystem.

The report examines five major market shifts shaping the sector: the militarization of space, the rise of hybrid sovereign-commercial architectures, increasing supplier diversity, growing emphasis on resilience and Space Domain Awareness, and rising demand for counterspace and sovereign defense capabilities.

The study includes analysis of seven capability domains, spending forecasts, industry revenue assessments, country profiles, multinational stakeholder coverage, and supporting datasets, providing strategic insight into one of the fastest-evolving segments of the global space economy.
